title: 3. Council of Ephesus (431)
about: Is Mary the Theotokos, the Mother of God? One Christ, not two.

items.text: Nestorius, archbishop of Constantinople, refused to call the Virgin Mary 'Theotokos' (she who gave birth to God). He spoke as if the Son of God and the man Jesus were two. St Cyril of Alexandria answered that the one born of Mary is the eternal Son Himself, made flesh.
Elizabeth calls Mary 'the mother of my Lord'. The Word did not join Himself to a man; He became flesh.
The council's acts include St Cyril's letters to Nestorius, which explain how the one Christ is both God and man.

items.father: The Council of Ephesus, with St Cyril's letters

items.text: About 200 bishops, led by St Cyril, deposed Nestorius and confessed Mary as Theotokos. The council also forbade anyone to put forward a different creed from that of Nicaea.
Every time we sing 'Most holy Theotokos, save us', we confess who her Son is. Honour given to the Mother is a confession of faith in Christ.
